title: Simplify TermAl project memory: consolidate operational rules into a small canonical set
outcome: Simplify TermAl project memory: consolidate operational rules into a small canonical set
acceptance: Every current project memory is audited and given one disposition, recorded in a note on this item: kept as a canonical entry, merged into a named canonical key, forgotten as obsolete (with the reason), or forgotten as superseded (naming the successor).

Greg's durable decisions keep their verbatim words and provenance, in their own entries or quoted inside the canonical entry that absorbs them; no authority, safety, review or restart rule is weakened, and each merged rule can be traced to the canonical key that now carries it.

Each workaround tied to an open item stays traceable to its retirement target: its operative line in the live exception list names the retiring item, and its full original text is a note on that item.
A note on this item reports the counts before and after and lists the resulting canonical keys, and Engram::Advisor is sent that report for Greg.

completion.summary:
TermAl project memory went from 97 keys to 14 canonical keys in two stages, each forgotten only after an independent read-only Codex audit passed:
- stage 1: 54 duplicates, audit round 4;
- stage 2: 42 keys, consolidated after one Medium was fixed and re-audited.
Every Greg quote is kept character-exact in greg-decisions-provenance. Each workaround's full text is a verbatim note on its retiring item, and live-workarounds keeps one line each. No repository text changed; memory content only. The report went to Engram::Advisor for Greg. The independent acceptance evaluation (delegation-20b8d7ca) passed 4/4. Closed by Termal::Fable2 under Greg's 2026-10-03 word that reversible tracker decisions need no confirmation from him (Advisor #185).
